prior_findings.limits: Architecture closure rests on the traced code and normative budget/ownership contract, not test counts. Pre-fix executions were not repeated. The claim that all three tests failed pre-fix is not independently substantiated: the relative-mode test is a compatibility control, and the pre-fix code already forwarded its duration unchanged after replacement. The two bounded-mode cases directly distinguish the stale-budget defect.

test_assertion_review: The round-2 test diff adds three tests and changes only the module-level fixture description; no pre-existing assertion is deleted, weakened or rewritten. The fixture adds a 2-second delay before hello only for worker_id slow-start (tests/fixtures/resident_worker_runtime.py:43); production worker code, wire framing and response shapes are untouched. The new assertions lock the normative separation between an absolute bounded dispatch and legacy relative execution duration, plus healthy-worker retention on pre-execution saturation. Both bounded expiry outcomes in the first test are legitimate: execution-time timeout if some budget remains after handshake, or no-execution saturation if startup exhausts it. Its generous-budget control prevents unconditional rejection from satisfying the test. The second test uses crash:eof as a no-dispatch sentinel and then proves reuse, rather than merely asserting an error code. The third preserves existing relative behavior instead of demanding the compatibility API adopt absolute timing. Focused --nocapture output showed all three passing with no Python-unavailable skip messages. The tests supplement source verification; they do not by themselves prove architecture compliance.
